chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, who said:

The young son of Muhammad ibn al-Hasan died and left behind a sister, and he bequeathed all his wealth to her. He said: So we sold his belongings and they amounted to one thousand dirhams, and they were brought to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). He said: And I wrote to him and informed him that he had bequeathed all his wealth to her. He said: So he took one-third of what I sent to him and returned the remainder, and ordered me to give it to her heir.
ai.seo_question: How did the Imam rule on a bequest of all wealth to an heir who also has a statutory inheritance share?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfabar illustrates the practical application of the rule that a bequest to an heir requires the consent of other heirs, as the Imam accepted one-third of the estate while returning the remainder to the sister. It highlights the distinction between the fixed statutory shares (fara'id) and the discretionary bequest (wasiyyah), emphasizing that the bequest is drawn from the estate before distribution. This case underscores the scholarly principle that an heir's bequest is valid but limited to one-third unless other heirs agree to more.
